protocol.name: ZeroFS
protocol.summary: ZeroFS is a high-performance POSIX filesystem and block-device abstraction layer engineered to interface directly with S3-compatible object storage backends, delivering microsecond-latency data access, kernel-level mounting capabilities, and mandatory always-on encryption.
protocol.constraints: ZeroFS must be used only as ephemeral I/O, never persistent storage. All mounted namespaces, cached metadata, and transient blocks are completely destroyed and overwritten upon execution lifecycle completion.

integration.type: Stateless, kernel-level storage abstraction integration acting exclusively as an ephemeral I/O loop buffer for sovereign runtime agents.
data_flows: Wnode sovereign compute agents dynamically spin up and mount transient ZeroFS block volumes at execution initialization via Fuse or native NBD hooks.

Data segments are pulled as encrypted objects from designated S3 buckets, decrypted inside isolated container memory spaces, modified during runtime, and instantly written back to destination objects.
The local mount path is hard-wiped using secure zeroization passes upon execution exit, ensuring zero persistence on the Wnode substrate.
security: End-to-end encryption leveraging AES-GCM-256 with ephemeral, single-use keys managed via secure enclave key generation layers.
Strict transient lifecycle management where volume termination triggers an automated file system dismantle and memory page purging loop.
Zero local long-term retention rules enforced by kernel-level monitoring mechanisms that block persistent write persistence.
No direct exposure of underlying raw S3 access credentials or backend infrastructure configurations to the execution runtime layers.

value_to_wnode.ephemeral_io: Allows Wnode to achieve strict compliance with zero-storage requirements while still offering agents native POSIX file operational interfaces (open, read, write, seek).
value_to_wnode.agent_workflows: Enables legacy compiled binaries, complex AI inference engines, and structural analysis pipelines to execute on Wnode by reading data streams through standard file descriptors.
value_to_wnode.performance: Mitigates typical object storage network latency overheads by leveraging localized microsecond-range caching layers contained within non-persistent RAM disks.

value_to_zerofs.new_volume: Generates massive, high-frequency transactional data stream traffic driven by millions of automated agent processing iterations running continuously.
value_to_zerofs.positioning: Establishes ZeroFS as the foundational, industry-standard stateless storage abstraction utility for decentralized physical infrastructure networks and sovereign computing grids.

agent_capabilities: Use block-device semantics for complex workloads
workflow_examples: An automated Wnode parsing agent mounts a transient ZeroFS path, streams down an encrypted dataset block, updates mathematical tables in isolated cache space, pushes output files to remote targets, and runs a mandatory file destruction sweep on exit.

Multiple distributed processing agents access shared, encrypted, transient ZeroFS network buffers to coordinate mid-point processing states, destroying the shared target mount immediately after output convergence.

drivers: High-frequency agent workloads executing continuous short-lived transactional data transformation tasks.
Enterprise compute pipelines requiring native POSIX compliance semantics to run legacy systems without modification.
Transient block-device operations and high-throughput vector scanning routines that bill per gigabyte processed per minute.
